column1: # RESULT 1 -- ACTION p374-A IS DISCHARGED, and the three draws are: NIL / PARTIAL / PARTIAL.
# 🔴 p373's "THE DECISIVE CELL" is the MINORITY draw at 1 of 3.  The claim it was built to
# support -- "English + organ = NIL for Germany, so German is NECESSARY" -- is NOT a stable
# property of the cell and no pass may cite cell 2 for it.
# 🔵 This is NOT a variance estimate.  n=3 on a non-deterministic tool establishes that the
# cell is non-deterministic; it does not say how often it returns which, and no frequency
# figure is published.  p375 declines to compute 2/3 as a rate.
# RESULT 2 -- AND IT IS THE STRONGER HALF: p374's SURVIVING ACCOUNT IS REFUTED FOR GERMANY,
# on a prediction registered before the search.
# 🔴 The French leg did not outperform the English leg.  Both legs reached THE SAME SINGLE
# OUTLET.  So for Germany the operative variable is NOT the language of the query: it is the
# EXISTENCE OF ONE PAGE, which both language legs happen to index.
# 🟢 What replaces it, and it fits all three Germany draws plus p374's Japan/Brazil/India cells:
# the unit is not a language and not a jurisdiction -- it is AN OUTLET.  A leg is productive
# when at least one indexed outlet covers that jurisdiction's education policy in ANY language
# the query can reach; the query's language matters only insofar as it changes WHICH outlets are
# reachable, and for Germany the reachable set has SIZE ONE in both languages tested.
# 🔴 The sharp consequence a successor must not soften: a jurisdiction served by ONE outlet is
# ONE OUTLET AWAY FROM A NIL, which is exactly why draw 1 returned nothing.  That is a
# FRAGILITY property of the jurisdiction's coverage, not a property of the query language.
# 🔴 STATED LIMITATIONS.
#   1. n=1 on F1.  One French draw cannot establish that French reaches only actuia.com.
#   2. "Same outlet" is measured as the same domain returning the same dated fact; the two
#      legs' full result sets differ in their NON-German items, which is not evidence either way.
